item.title: Open-source replacements used to mean settling for less, but the ones I switched to this year are just better
item.dc:creator: Nolen Jonker
item.description: Paid apps have some catching up to do
item.content:encoded: It used to be the case that choosing an open-source app over the paid version came with an unspoken deal. You skip the subscription in exchange for an interface that looks like it's from ten years ago, and spend your evenings on forums trying to figure out why a feature isn't behaving. Many are actually perfectly fine with that trade, myself included to an extent.

item.title: Amazon's Fire TV Stick 4K Plus drops to just $29.99, and it's a steal for 4K streaming
item.dc:creator: XDA Deals Desk
item.description: Wi-Fi 6, Dolby Vision, and a steep discount
item.content:encoded: If you've been meaning to turn an older TV into a smart one, or your current streaming stick has started to lag, this one is worth a look. Now you can get the Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus for $29.99 as part of an early Black Friday deal, down from its regular price of $69.99 on Amazon.

item.title: My Raspberry Pi Pico 2 lacks an OS and onboard network features, yet it’s more reliable than every Pi in my house for one task
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Kumar Mishra
item.description: A headless Pico2 transformed into a tiny web dashboard via USB NCM and Arduino-Pico, serving live Docker metrics.
item.content:encoded: Raspberry Pi has launched multiple boards and even different series in the last ten years. You might be familiar with the mainstream Raspberry Pi boards like the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B or Raspberry Pi 5. In addition, you can pick the Raspberry Pi Zero series, which is best for single-purpose roles, and the Raspberry Pi Pico series, which is for embedded computing. I have a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, and recently bought a Raspberry Pi Pico board as well. I intended to find time to learn electronics and circuitry. But I didn't find the time or purpose for it, even after a month of having it.
